{{Quote|I left for the Unknown Regions, determined to lose myself. I learned that ''unknown'' was not the same as ''empty''.|[[Darth Krayt]]|<ref name="Legacy 18">[[Legacy (2006) 18|''Legacy'' (2006) 18]]</ref>}}
The '''Unknown Regions''', also known as '''Unknown Space''',<ref name="ME">{{JournalCite|7|Mist Encounter}}</ref> the '''Unknown Sector''',<ref name="XW:RS">''[[X-Wing: Rogue Squadron]]''</ref> the '''Unknown Reaches''',<ref name="Endgame">{{DarkStryder|adventure=Endgame (adventure)|book=Endgame}}</ref> the '''Unknown Territories''',<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref> or the '''Unexplored Regions''',<ref name="TLCS">''[[The Last Command Sourcebook]]''</ref> was a region located in the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] west beyond the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. The Unknown Regions were largely unexplored, in contrast to [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]], which was explored.<ref name="TEA" />

The Unknown Regions was broadly defined as areas not connected with the skein of reliable or well-known [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace routes]] spanning the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] and did not belong to the wider well-known [[galactic community]] of look to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] as the ultimate center of civilization, or were not part of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. 

==History==
{{Quote|There are a hundred different threats out there that would freeze your blood if you knew about them.|[[Kres'ten'tarthi|Stent]] to [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]]|<ref name="VotF">''[[Vision of the Future]]''</ref>}}
The reach of civilization extended at least nominally to the edge of the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] disk&mdash;for instance, the territory of the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]] extended to the end of the [[Tingel Arm/Legends|Tingel Arm]]. The galactic disk and some satellite galaxies were mapped well enough that the omission of thirty-seven systems (including [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]) from stellar charts were obvious gravitational anomalies, even when scanning from afar.

The large galactic volume designated as the "Unknown Regions" included uncharted areas in dense [[Nebula/Legends|nebulae]], globular clusters, and the galactic halos. 15% of the galaxy's stellar mass was estimated to be contained within the Unknown Regions.<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic II: Refugee">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic II: Refugee]]''</ref><ref name="TEA" /> Many governments repeatedly sent scouts into the Unknown Regions. [[General/Legends|General]] [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] once remarked that "If [[New Republic/Legends|you]] continue to map the Unknown Regions, you'll have to call them something else."<ref name="adumar">''[[X-Wing: Starfighters of Adumar]]''</ref> During the early years of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], a colonization corporation, [[Anawa]], offered refuge to people by guiding them into the Unknown Regions where the corporation would administrate and police newly discovered habitable planets.<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref>

The Unknown Regions included a unique section of the galactic disk to the "galactic west" of [[Bakura/Legends|Bakura]], [[Bilbringi system/Legends|Bilbringi]], and the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]]. Important powers in this area of space included the [[Chiss Ascendancy/Legends|Chiss Ascendancy]], the [[Ssi-ruuvi Imperium]], the [[Vagaari/Legends|Vagaari]], the [[Killik/Legends|Killik]] [[The Colony|Colony]], and the [[Empire of the Hand]], but it was also home to species such as the [[Croke]], the [[Ebruchi]] and the [[Eickarie]]. Though severely cut off from the rest of the galaxy, these species interacted with one another, and had created a sort of interstellar culture separate of that of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] or the Empire. Communication and trade were sparse and infrequent, but species such as the [[Lugubraa]] were found in the services of larger powers across the Regions. Common threats such as [[Mnggal-Mnggal]] brought together disparate species such as the Chiss, Lugubraa, and others to combat its encroachments.<ref name="TUR" />

[[File:Terminus_ground.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The spaceports on [[Terminus/Legends|Terminus]] had ships going to and from the Unknown Regions.]]

One hypothesis by a noted [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] suggested that a mass of dark matter intersected the galaxy in this region, creating gravitational anomalies that hindered navigation. However, the lack of any tidal disruption of the galaxy's spiral form (as shown in [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]]) may have disproved this supposed dark mass. Alternate theories included "hyperspatial gravitic ripples", or the intentional construction of a barrier, possibly by the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]] to hedge the expanding [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] or to contain [[Mnggal-Mnggal]]. What was known for certain is that<ref name="TEA" /> a web of [[Hyperspace anomaly/Legends|hyperspace anomalies]] known as "[[Western barrier|the tangle]]"<ref name="TUR" /> that impeded galactic exploration by the Republic for millennia and divided explored space and the Regions was almost precisely at the midline of the [[circumferential hyperspace barrier]] that surrounded the galaxy.<ref name="TEA" /> It was clear, moreover, that much of the Unknown Regions were passable to determined travelers&mdash;for instance, [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] traders had been in contact with the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] for many years before their "re-discovery,"<ref name="OBF">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']]</ref> the planet [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]] was reachable by [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] navigators,<ref name="TEA" /> the Rakata homeworld of [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]] was also reached by a [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic naval]] task force at the climax of the [[Jedi Civil War]]<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> and subsequently made a protected historical site by the Republic. Additionally, frontier spaceport worlds in the known galaxy, like [[Terminus/Legends|Terminus]], were known to be visited frequently by transports and traders from the Unknown Regions.<ref name="TEA" />

[[Iokath]], was a massive artificial sphere that constructed weapons. The [[Nihil Retreat]] was a collection of twelve stellar clusters associated with the [[Perann Nebula/Legends|Perann Nebula]], that housed the planet [[Rhand]]. In some eras, like during the [[Great Galactic War]], [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] and [[Galactic War]], prominent species like the Chiss cooperated with galactic powers like the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]].<ref name="TORHp">{{HolonetOld|inhabitants|chiss|Chiss}}</ref> The Ascendancy also participated in diplomatic talks with the Republic<ref name="TCWSM2">''[[The Clone Wars: Secret Missions 2: Curse of the Black Hole Pirates]]''</ref> and later maintained relations with both the Galactic Empire,<ref name="TUR" /> the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> and the second [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]] ruled by [[Darth Krayt]].<ref name="SWL15">[[Legacy (2006) 15|''Legacy'' (2006) 15]]</ref>

===Imperial exploration===
As part of the relations with the Galactic Empire, the Chiss Imperial [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], a native of these parts, was dispatched aboard the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Admonitor]]'' to the Unknown Regions during the years of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], ostensibly on a simple mapping expedition, but in reality to explore and subjugate entire sectors for the Galactic Empire. While there, Thrawn appeared to have encountered the extragalactic [[Yuuzhan Vong]]. He also created a shadow Empire, the [[Empire of the Hand]]. Thrawn would establish military installations, shipyards, and laboratories. Normalized relations between the Chiss Ascendancy and the New Republic were established following the Galactic Civil War, and the portion of the Unknown Regions existing in the galactic disk was essentially eliminated thanks to the availability of Chiss [[Star map/Legends|star-charts]].<ref name="TEA" /> At least several [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnoughts]] were sent to the Unknown Regions by Emperor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> By [[21 ABY/Legends|21 ABY]], the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] ''[[Intimidator (Executor-class)|Intimidator]] ''of the [[Black Fleet]] would be discovered after a [[Black Fleet Crisis|long crisis]], only in battle remains.

==Sectors==
Due to the very fact that the region was "unknown," it presumably had not been charted and divided into sectors by the Republic. However, the Empire of the Hand had plotted 250 sectors in the region.

==Behind the scenes==
The depiction of the Unknown Regions varies from source to source. In ''[[Vision of the Future]]'', the space known to the Old Republic, Empire, and New Republic is not specifically assigned to any section of the galactic disk, nor are the Unknown Regions. They do appear adjacent on the map, which includes the disk. The territory under the hegemony of the Empire of the Hand, while by no means comprising all of the Unknown Regions, seemingly embraces as much as 240 [[Sector/Legends|sectors]], roughly a quarter of the volume of known space. Although huge, this volume is emptier than the galactic disk, since the combined total of the Unknown Regions contains no more than one percent of the galaxy's stars.<ref>''[[Galaxy Guide 8: Scouts]]'' p24; ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]'' p301</ref>

In contrast, [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']] and [[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|''The New Jedi Order'']] series, as well as the associated galactic map, have bulked the Unknown Regions on one side of the galactic disk.

Recent sources such as ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' and ''[[The Unknown Regions]]'' incorporate both interpretations of the region, ascribing the internal galactic portion to the result of an initially impassable hyperspace barrier near the mid-line of the galaxy, in addition to the one located beyond the edge of the galactic disk, with the area beyond that known as the Intergalactic Void.
